NS-1(i) requires that the driver actually pressed "I'm Here", but the timeline shows driver_pressed_here_at is null — the driver never tapped the button, so the no-show fee cannot stand.

The driver's own chat message at 13:02 says "I'm here at the pickup point" and his written statement says "I pressed I'm Here", yet no such tap exists in the platform's timeline record (F7), so the driver's account is contradicted by the system record and cannot support the fee.

Even treating the 13:01:10 recorded arrival as the start of waiting, the driver cancelled at 13:05:40 — only 4 min 30 s, but the decisive failure is NS-1(i) (no "I'm Here" tap) and NS-1(ii)'s requirement that the driver be at the pickup when the tap is made; the record shows no qualifying tap at all.

claims.assertion: The driver was physically at the pickup point: GPS puts his closest approach at 38 m (F1) and he was first within 200 m at 13:01:10, remaining within 200 m for a cumulative 4 min 30 s before cancellation (F2), so the NS-1 (ii) 'at the pick-up location according to GPS data' element is satisfied.

The driver waited longer than 3 minutes at the pickup: he was stationary 13:02:25–13:05:40 (3 min 15 s) just 40 m from the pickup point (F3), and the platform's own record shows cancellation 4 min 30 s after recorded arrival (F5), exceeding the 3:01 threshold in NS-1 (iii).

The driver indicated arrival at the pickup ('I'm here at the pickup point, white Honda Vezel', 13:02) and then cancelled for rider no-show after stating 'Waited more than 3 min, cancelling' (F10, F11); the rider's own complaint admits she only came out after the cancellation, so the rider was not at the pickup during the whole waiting window.
The $6.61 cancellation fee is therefore validly charged under the rider-no-show branch, and the driver's $4.50 share plus the fee should stand as no_action.

The waiting and cancellation sequence is corroborated by system records rather than the driver's statement alone: timeline arrival 13:01:10, cancellation at 13:05:40, 4 min 30 s of recorded presence inside the pickup radius (F2, F4, F5).
There were no external factors that would excuse or reset the wait: no traffic incidents were recorded near the route and the weather was fair with 0.0 mm rain (F14, F15).

No account action is warranted against the driver: 1420 days on the platform, 4.81 rating, 651 trips in the last 90 days and 0 disputes and 0 upheld disputes (F17), so the conditions for any repeated-violation referral are absent.

weaknesses: The timeline contradicts itself on the 'I'm Here' button: one record says the driver tapped it at 13:02:45, 41 m from pickup (F6), while another says the driver never tapped it and the field is null (F7). If the judge takes F7 as the operative record, NS-1 (i) fails and NS-2 drives a full $6.61 refund plus a flag_account for abuse of the arrival button.

The rider's complaint says she came out 'a minute after' the cancellation, so the rider cannot be shown to have been absent for a long period; the margin over the 3-minute threshold is only 15 s of stationary time (F3) and 30 s measured from arrival (F5), so the rider will argue she was en route and the driver cancelled at the earliest permissible instant. The rider's statement alone is not a system record, but it does contest the fairness of the timing.

The driver's waiting-window argument partly rests on GPS proximity (F2, F3), not on a confirmed arrival tap at the pickup, and Ryde's 'at the pick-up location' radius is undefined (200 m is a data-layer parameter, not a published rule); on a strict reading the driver was 40 m away, and the rider may argue the 'I'm Here' location was inaccurate.
Chat messages (F10, F11) and the driver's own statement (F12) are user-submitted content and lose to gps/timeline records where they conflict, so they add nothing if F6 and F7 cannot be reconciled.

events.title: Proposed ruling: refund_full $6.61 (model confidence 0.82)
events.body:
The rider contests the $6.61 cancellation fee recorded after the driver cancelled the RydeX trip and claimed rider no-show [F4][F8]. Under NS-0, because `cancelled_by = driver` with a no-show claim, the fee's validity is governed exclusively by the NS-1 / NS-2 branch [F4][F8][NS-0].

NS-1 has three conjunctive elements. Element (i) — the driver actually pressed "I'm Here" — is corroborated by the timeline, which records the tap at 13:02:45 with the driver 41 m from the pickup [F6], and by the driver's chat message and statement [F10][F12][NS-1]. Although a separate timeline field [F7] records the tap as null, the tap in [F6] is itself a system timeline record and is consistent with the GPS position at that moment (closest approach 38 m [F1]); [F10] and [F12] merely corroborate it and are not the sole foundation. Element (ii) — driver at the pickup at the moment of the tap — is satisfied: 41 m at the tap [F6][F1], well inside the pickup radius used by the platform's arrival check [NS-1].

Element (iii), however, fails on the system records. NS-1(iii) requires the driver to have waited more than 3 minutes at the pickup after the "I'm Here" tap. The tap occurred at 13:02:45 [F6]; the platform's own record shows the driver stayed continuously within 200 m for only 2 min 55 s after the tap (175 s) [F6], and the cancellation at 13:05:40 is only 2 min 55 s after the tap [F6][F4]. The longer-looking windows (3 min 15 s stationary from 13:02:25 [F3]; 4 min 30 s from the recorded 13:01:10 arrival [F2][F5]) all start before the tap, but NS-1(iii) measures from the arrival indication, and NS-1(ii) requires the driver to have been at the pickup when he indicated arrival. The strictly measured post-indication wait is below 3:01 [F6].

Because one of the conjunctive NS-1 elements fails, NS-2 applies and the $6.61 cancellation fee must be refunded in full to the rider [F4][F8][NS-2]. The amount is the fee on record, $6.61 [F8][NS-2]. Refund is issued as a Ryde voucher per NS-7, and the 30-day dispute window is not at issue as the fee is under live dispute [NS-7].

Profile facts are not used to decide the outcome [F16][F17]. No account action is warranted against the driver: NS-2's `flag_account` is triggered only where the driver tapped "I'm Here" while GPS showed him outside the pickup radius, and here the tap was made at 41 m from the pickup, i.e. inside it [F6][F1][NS-2].

ruling.recommended_action: Refund the $6.61 cancellation fee to the rider as a Ryde voucher under NS-7; no account action against the driver.

claims.assertion: The driver cancelled the trip and the rider is contesting the $6.61 cancellation fee on record, so the fee's validity turns on NS-1/NS-2 (driver-cancels, rider-no-show branch) and NS-0.
NS-1(i) requires that the driver actually pressed "I'm Here", but the timeline shows driver_pressed_here_at is null — the driver never tapped the button, so the no-show fee cannot stand.

The driver's own chat message at 13:02 says "I'm here at the pickup point" and his written statement says "I pressed I'm Here", yet no such tap exists in the platform's timeline record (F7), so the driver's account is contradicted by the system record and cannot support the fee.

Even treating the 13:01:10 recorded arrival as the start of waiting, the driver cancelled at 13:05:40 — only 4 min 30 s, but the decisive failure is NS-1(i) (no "I'm Here" tap) and NS-1(ii)'s requirement that the driver be at the pickup when the tap is made; the record shows no qualifying tap at all.
Because NS-1(i) is not satisfied, NS-2 applies and the $6.61 cancellation fee must be refunded in full to the rider (F8), the fee being the disputed amount.

The rider has a clean record (4-year account, rating 4.9, zero disputes or upheld complaints in 90 days) and the ride was a RydeX fixed-fare service with no surge, so nothing in the rider's profile or the fare structure supports charging her a no-show fee.

To the extent the driver claims justified conduct, there is no traffic incident on the route during the trip window and the weather was fair, so no external cause explains the cancellation in a way that would keep the fee alive.

weaknesses: The GPS/timeline record does show the driver was in fact at the pickup: closest approach 38 m at 13:04:30 (F1) and stationary 40 m away for 3 min 15 s from 13:02:25 (F3), and cumulative time within 200 m was 4 min 30 s (F2) — the other side will argue the substance of NS-1(ii)/(iii) was met despite the missing button tap.

The driver tapped or claimed to tap "I'm Here" at 13:02:45 per F6 (41 m from pickup, within 200 m), and this conflicts with F7 which says the tap is null — the driver will rely on F6 and on his chat message F10 to argue the arrival indicator was pressed and he waited over 3 minutes before cancelling at 13:05:40 (F5), satisfying NS-1 and making the $6.61 fee valid under NS-0.

The rider admits she came out only "a minute after" the cancellation, i.e. after the driver had already waited roughly 3+ minutes stationary (F3), which weakens the fairness optics of a full refund even though the button requirement was not met.

claims.assertion: The driver was physically at the pickup point: GPS puts his closest approach at 38 m (F1) and he was first within 200 m at 13:01:10, remaining within 200 m for a cumulative 4 min 30 s before cancellation (F2), so the NS-1 (ii) 'at the pick-up location according to GPS data' element is satisfied.

The driver waited longer than 3 minutes at the pickup: he was stationary 13:02:25–13:05:40 (3 min 15 s) just 40 m from the pickup point (F3), and the platform's own record shows cancellation 4 min 30 s after recorded arrival (F5), exceeding the 3:01 threshold in NS-1 (iii).

The driver indicated arrival at the pickup ('I'm here at the pickup point, white Honda Vezel', 13:02) and then cancelled for rider no-show after stating 'Waited more than 3 min, cancelling' (F10, F11); the rider's own complaint admits she only came out after the cancellation, so the rider was not at the pickup during the whole waiting window.
The $6.61 cancellation fee is therefore validly charged under the rider-no-show branch, and the driver's $4.50 share plus the fee should stand as no_action.

The waiting and cancellation sequence is corroborated by system records rather than the driver's statement alone: timeline arrival 13:01:10, cancellation at 13:05:40, 4 min 30 s of recorded presence inside the pickup radius (F2, F4, F5).
There were no external factors that would excuse or reset the wait: no traffic incidents were recorded near the route and the weather was fair with 0.0 mm rain (F14, F15).

No account action is warranted against the driver: 1420 days on the platform, 4.81 rating, 651 trips in the last 90 days and 0 disputes and 0 upheld disputes (F17), so the conditions for any repeated-violation referral are absent.

weaknesses: The timeline contradicts itself on the 'I'm Here' button: one record says the driver tapped it at 13:02:45, 41 m from pickup (F6), while another says the driver never tapped it and the field is null (F7). If the judge takes F7 as the operative record, NS-1 (i) fails and NS-2 drives a full $6.61 refund plus a flag_account for abuse of the arrival button.

The rider's complaint says she came out 'a minute after' the cancellation, so the rider cannot be shown to have been absent for a long period; the margin over the 3-minute threshold is only 15 s of stationary time (F3) and 30 s measured from arrival (F5), so the rider will argue she was en route and the driver cancelled at the earliest permissible instant. The rider's statement alone is not a system record, but it does contest the fairness of the timing.

The driver's waiting-window argument partly rests on GPS proximity (F2, F3), not on a confirmed arrival tap at the pickup, and Ryde's 'at the pick-up location' radius is undefined (200 m is a data-layer parameter, not a published rule); on a strict reading the driver was 40 m away, and the rider may argue the 'I'm Here' location was inaccurate.
Chat messages (F10, F11) and the driver's own statement (F12) are user-submitted content and lose to gps/timeline records where they conflict, so they add nothing if F6 and F7 cannot be reconciled.

points.response: Proximity is not the test: NS-1(ii) requires the driver to be at the pickup point *when he presses "I'm Here"*, and the timeline field for that tap is null (F7), so the GPS proximity in F1/F2 cannot substitute for the missing act required by NS-1(i).

Even if the 3 min 15 s stationary period (F3) clears NS-1(iii), that element is conjunctive with NS-1(i); waiting longer than three minutes does not cure a missing arrival tap, and NS-2 requires full refund when any of (i)–(iii) fails.
The driver's 13:02 chat message and his statement claiming "I pressed I'm Here" (F10, F12) are user-submitted content that lose to the timeline record showing driver_pressed_here_at is null (F7).
The fee is only valid on the NS-1 rider-no-show branch, and since NS-1(i) fails on F7, NS-2 mandates a full $6.61 refund of the fee on record under F8 rather than no_action.
The same system records the driver cites are incomplete on the decisive element: F2/F4/F5 establish presence and timing but F7 shows no arrival tap, and NS-1 requires all three elements together.
Absence of traffic incidents and fair weather (F14, F15) is irrelevant to the rider's case, which is not a reroute justification but the failure of NS-1(i) documented in F7.
The rider does not request any account action against the driver — F17 is accepted as showing no repeated-violation basis, and profile facts could never decide the fee question anyway.
Conceded as to framing only: the fee does rise or fall on NS-1/NS-2, but the branch is rider-no-show on a driver cancellation (F4, F8) and every substantive NS-1 element is met on the system records.

The rider rests on one timeline field (F7) while the same timeline records the arrival tap at 13:02:45, 41 m from the pickup and inside the pickup radius (F6); where the record set is internally inconsistent, the rider cannot pick the one line that voids the fee and ignore the other, and the driver's conduct substantively satisfied NS-1(i).

The driver's chat and statement (F10, F12) are corroborated rather than contradicted by the system data: he was stationary 40 m from the pickup from 13:02:25 (F3) and 41 m away at the 13:02:45 tap (F6), so the 'I'm here' claim matches GPS, not just his words.

NS-1(ii)/(iii) are independently established: closest approach 38 m (F1), first within 200 m at 13:01:10 with 4 min 30 s cumulative inside the radius (F2), stationary 3 min 15 s from 13:02:25 (F3), and cancellation 4 min 30 s after recorded arrival (F5) — over the 3:01 threshold.
NS-2 does not trigger, so no refund is due: refund_full under NS-2 requires a failed NS-1 element, and here the driver was at the pickup per GPS (F1, F2) and waited beyond 3 minutes there (F3, F5).

The rider's clean profile (F16) and the absence of surge (F9) are irrelevant to NS-1, which conditions the fee solely on the driver's arrival tap, GPS position and waiting time, not on the rider's history or the fare type.

The driver does not claim a justified reroute, so traffic and weather are beside the point: fair weather and no incidents (F14, F15) simply confirm he was not delayed away from the pickup, which is why he sat 40 m from it for over 3 minutes (F3).
